titleText.es: Al final se funda la ONU. Y luego un rebelde solitario arría toda la fila de banderas de delante de la fachada, corre hasta su base, y consigue tropecientos millones de puntos.
titleText.en: Eventually a UN is set up. And then a lone rebel runs down the line of flags in front of it, runs back to his base, and gets a kajillion points.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive translates the capture-the-flag continuation freely: it explicitly says that the rebel lowers the whole row of flags and uses the playful number tropecientos millones for the enormous score.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Derrocó is a completed-past form for one person, group, or state.
Su does not show the owner's gender. Here a singular institution or place is the owner.
Before a noun, antiguo often means former or previous rather than physically old.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: order; established social or political system
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Orden is masculine when it means an arrangement, command, or established system.

example.es: El cambio alteró el orden político.
example.en: The change altered the political order.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estableció is a completed-past form for one person, group, or institution.

example.es: El país estableció un nuevo sistema.
example.en: The country established a new system.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Constitucional has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.
Firmaron is firmar's completed-past form for more than one person.
Here tratado is a noun naming an agreement between governments, not the completed form of tratar.

example.es: Los dos países aprobaron el tratado.
example.en: The two countries approved the treaty.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: were left; ended up (in a resulting state)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A form of quedar can introduce the state that remains after an event. The following completed-action form describes that state.
The -as ending matches more than one feminine thing being described.
In a diplomatic context, acuerdos can name formal agreements between governments.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: they said; they used to say
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Decían is an imperfect-past form for repeated, ongoing, or background speech by more than one person.

example.en: Many people used to say it was impossible.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: To make this ‘would’ form, tener changes to the irregular base tendr- and adds -ía. The following noun states what would be had.

example.es: El proyecto tendría un coste alto.
example.en: The project would have a high cost.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Aplazado describes something moved to a later time.
Ondea is a present-time form for one flag or other thing moving in waves.

example.es: La bandera ondea sobre el edificio.
example.en: The flag flies over the building.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Orgullosa matches a feminine singular thing. With a verb of movement or appearance, English may express the same idea with an adverb such as proudly.
Here ellos is the subject that performs the following action.
In a political or geographic context, tierras can mean a people's territory rather than separate pieces of soil.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: any; at all (after a noun in a negative setting)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Alguno normally means some before a noun. After a noun and following a negative word such as sin, it strengthens the negative meaning.

example.en: She did it without any problem at all.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Abandona tells one familiar person to leave something behind.
Reunirse uses reúne for the positive command to one familiar person, and te is attached at the end because the action is joining or meeting with others. The written accent preserves the stress.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links es hora to the action whose time has come
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After es hora, use de before an action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
After a negative statement, sino replaces the rejected option with a contrasting one.

example.en: I do not want to run, but rather to walk.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: in; among (introducing what ‘best’ or ‘worst’ is compared across)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After a highest-or-lowest description such as el mejor or el peor, de can introduce the full group or time range being compared.

example.es: Es la mejor canción de la década.
example.en: It is the best song of the decade.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: cosa + quedar + participio que describe el resultado
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can quedar describe the state left by a completed action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Name the thing, use the matching form of quedar, and add the completed-action form with an ending that matches the thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: For example, la puerta quedó cerrada and las reglas quedaron establecidas describe the resulting states of the door and rules.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something has no end?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use no, a matching form of tener, and fin.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The form of tener changes with the subject and time: no tiene fin, no tendría fin, no tuvo fin.

example.es: La espera parecía no tener fin.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can alguno or alguna strengthen a negative after a noun?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the negative word first, then the noun, and put alguno or alguna after that noun.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This formal or emphatic order means ‘any ... at all’: sin temor alguno, no existe razón alguna.

example.en: He showed no interest at all.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone meets up with or joins another person?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of reunirse followed by con and the person or group.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short pronoun changes with the subject: me reúno, te reúnes, se reúne, nos reunimos. In a positive command it attaches to the end: reúnete.

example.en: We met up with the team.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: es hora de + verbo en forma de diccionario
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that it is time to do something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use es hora de, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Negation and contrast can surround the action: es hora no de discutir, sino de decidir.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: no + opción A, sino + opción B
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you reject one option and replace it with another?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put no before the rejected option and sino before its replacement.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Repeat a required preposition when both options need it: no de correr, sino de caminar.

example.en: We are not looking for excuses, but rather solutions.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you say that something is the best or worst ever?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a highest-or-lowest form such as el mejor, el peor, or el más largo, then add de la historia.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A highest-or-lowest form is called a superlative. De la historia sets all of history as its comparison range; natural English often uses ‘ever’ or ‘in history.’

example.es: Fue el partido más largo de la historia.
example.en: It was the longest game ever.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: banderas · fronteras · servidor de capturar la bandera
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the final complaint reinterpret the diplomatic speech?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Capture the flag is a team game in which players enter opposing territory, take a flag, and return it to their base. The solemn kingdoms, borders, embassies, flags, and peace appeal are revealed as role-play on a badly designed game server.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The title text continues the game logic with a rebel collecting a row of flags and returning to base for an enormous score.

excludedUnits.rationale: Liate is the unchanged invented kingdom name rather than a Spanish lexical word.

applications.explanationEn: Hace comes before the amount tres años to place the event three years before the present.
The noun monarquía comes first and constitucional follows it as the description.
Constitucional is singular to match monarquía and has the same singular form with either gender.
Derrocó presents the overthrow as one completed historical event.
Estableció presents the creation of the new system as a completed event.
Firmaron presents the treaty signing as a completed event by several people.
Quedaron presents the setting of the borders as a completed historical result.
Fronteras names the things, quedaron introduces the resulting state, and establecidas describes that state with a feminine plural ending.
Establecidas has the feminine plural ending -as to match fronteras.

No negates the prediction, tendría is tener's ‘would have’ form, and fin names the absent end.

applications.explanationEn: Ven is the irregular positive command telling one familiar person to come.
Abandona is the positive command telling one familiar person to leave something behind.
Reúnete is a positive command addressed to one familiar person.
The short pronoun te attaches to the end of the positive command reúne, and the written accent preserves the original stress.
Reúnete is the command form with te attached, con is required before the other party, and nosotros names that group.

applications.exampleEs: ES HORA NO DE LUCHAR, SINO DE VIVIR
applications.explanationEn: Es hora frames the moment to act; each de introduces one unchanged action verb, while the surrounding contrast rejects luchar and selects vivir.

applications.exampleEs: NO DE LUCHAR, SINO DE VIVIR
applications.explanationEn: No rejects the first de plus action, and sino introduces the replacement with the required de repeated.

applications.exampleEs: EL PEOR SERVIDOR DE CAPTURE-THE-FLAG DE LA HISTORIA
applications.explanationEn: El and peor mark servidor as the lowest-ranked member of the group, while de la historia sets all of history as the comparison range—natural English can express this as ‘ever.’
